## Bounded-scope decisions (recorded honestly)

- **S-size budget exceeded (~2,050 non-fixture lines vs ≤1,500).** The
  three reviewed parsers + the S7 screen land as one cohesive unit; a
  mid-run split would break the ACQ-24 seat set. Per the contract's own
  text the budget clause stops binding when exceeded — recorded, never
  smoothed.
- **Author names dropped, count kept.** Bill authors are legislators in
  public role, but Part VIII's person-naming default-deny binds: no
  author-name claim or entity field — the count rides the entity row
  (`author_count`, `authors_redacted`), the tab label `Autores (N)`
  supplies it on detail pages.
- **S7 drop is name-level, not row-level.** A non-organisation-shaped
  Contratista (person or merely untyped) mints no seller and never lands
  as a datum anywhere; the contract record itself still mints — the
  served row is real public data, the person name is the dropped datum
  (`contractor_screen`, `contractor_names_dropped` on the outcome row).
- **OCPR is pointer + conditional-contract emit.** The only committed
  OCPR surface is the landing page: FY links → pointers; a populated
  results table parses when served (today it ships empty — the POST form
  is never submitted, the FY download 404s). `ocpr_results.html` is a
  marked CONSTRUCTED fixture exercising the screen, never presented as a
  real capture.
- **`filed_date` is the documented normalization** of the served
  MM/DD/YYYY literals to ISO 8601; the verbatim literal stays in
  `filed_date_raw`/`raw_value`.
